userStories.title: Humanize story status labels — replace 'retry' with meaningful states
userStories.description: In PipelineMonitorPanel.tsx stories tab (lines ~1271-1273), the raw 'retry' DB status is shown as plain text. Stories with status='retry' are stories that failed in a prior run and are queued for re-execution in the current retry run. This label is confusing. Fix: add a STATUS_LABELS mapping in the component that translates internal status strings to human-readable labels with appropriate colors. 'retry' → show as 'Re-running' with an amber/orange badge style. While a story is the currently executing one (inferred from SSE story_started + story WAL events matching the storyId), highlight that row with a left accent border (3px, var(--accent)) and show an animated spinner badge 'In progress'. Use this mapping: pass → green 'Done', fail → red 'Failed', retry → amber 'Re-running', pending → muted 'Pending', skipped → teal 'Already Passing'. Each status uses a consistent badge shape (inline-flex items-center px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[10px] font-medium rounded border). The currently active story is tracked via usePipelineSSE events — when a story_started event fires, record that storyId in a ref and highlight that row. Clear the active story ID when story_passed or story_failed fires for that ID.
acceptanceCriteria: No story row displays the raw text 'retry' — it shows 'Re-running' with amber styling
Story with status 'pass' shows green 'Done' badge
Story with status 'fail' shows red 'Failed' badge
Story with status 'pending' shows muted 'Pending' badge
Story with status 'skipped' shows teal 'Already Passing' badge (unchanged from current)
The currently executing story (last story_started WAL event) has a 3px left accent border and animated spinner 'In progress' badge
Active story indicator clears when story_passed or story_failed fires for that storyId
All status badges use consistent sizing (text-[10px], px-1.5 py-0.5, rounded, border)

userStories.title: Per-story rerun button in Dive stories tab
userStories.description: The backend endpoint POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/retry already accepts an optional storyIds: string[] array (backend/src/routes/pipeline.ts lines ~2948-3092). The frontend only exposes 'Retry Failed' for all failures at once. Add individual story rerun buttons. In the stories tab, add a small RotateCcw icon button (size=12) on the far right of each story row. Show this button only when: (1) liveRun.status is 'done', 'failed', or 'partial_failure' (run is complete — never show during active run to avoid confusion), AND (2) story.status is 'fail' or 'failed'. On click: call POST /api/pipeline/runs/${selectedRunId}/retry with body { storyIds: [story.storyId], workspaceId }. Track per-story loading state in a Map<storyId, boolean> ref. On success, call setSelectedRunId(result.runId) to navigate to the new retry run. On error, show toast 'Failed to rerun story'. Button appears on row hover (opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 transition). Add group className to the story row button element.
acceptanceCriteria: Story row shows a RotateCcw rerun button on hover when run is completed (done/failed/partial_failure)
Button is completely hidden while run status is 'running' or 'paused'
Button only appears for stories with status 'fail' (not for pass/pending/skipped)
Clicking calls POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/retry with storyIds: [storyId]
Per-story loading spinner shows on that specific story's button during the API call
On success, setSelectedRunId transitions to the new runId
On error, toast shows 'Failed to rerun story'
Button has tooltip 'Rerun this story' (title attribute)
Existing 'Retry Failed' (retry-all) button in the header is unchanged

userStories.title: Tokens tab — fix empty state and add tab count badge
userStories.description: The Tokens tab in PipelineMonitorPanel.tsx exists (lines ~1366-1463) and is correctly implemented, but when no stories have recorded token data it appears completely blank — no message, no explanation. Fix: (1) Add a proper empty state: if totalInputTokens === 0 && totalOutputTokens === 0 && all stories have no token data, show a centered message: 'No token data yet — tokens are recorded as each story completes. If token counts never appear, ensure your execution engine reports usage (OpenCode and Anthropic API report tokens; Claude subscription usage may vary).' Include a Zap icon from lucide-react. (2) Update the Tokens tab label in the tabs array to show a count badge when data exists: change label from 'Tokens' to 'Tokens' with badge showing formatted total if > 0 (e.g., '124K'). The formatted total should use a helper like formatTokens() that already exists in the component. (3) The Tokens tab should not show the badge when total is 0 to avoid confusing '0' badge.
acceptanceCriteria: When no stories have token data, Tokens tab body shows centered empty state with Zap icon and explanatory message
Empty state message does NOT show '0 tokens' summary cards — only shows the message
When token data exists, the tab label shows a badge: 'Tokens · 124K' or similar
Tab badge only appears when total tokens > 0
Existing token summary cards and per-story chart are unchanged (no regression)
Empty state uses consistent styling with other empty states in the panel (text-muted, centered, icon + text)

userStories.title: Stories tab visual polish — left status border, badge system, and layout cleanup
userStories.description: Redesign the story row in PipelineMonitorPanel for a cleaner, more polished look. Current issues: status is unstyled plain text, row elements create visual noise, escalation/reroute badges clutter the collapsed row. Changes to make in the stories tab row (the <button> element for each story): (1) Add a 4px left border to each story row div, color-coded by status: pass=border-success, fail=border-error, retry=border-amber-500, pending=border-border, skipped=border-teal-500. The border should be on the wrapping div, not the button itself, so it doesn't affect click area. (2) Move escalation badges (Escalated: Haiku→Sonnet) and reroute badges into the expanded detail section only — remove them from the collapsed row view. They create clutter when 7+ stories all show escalation. (3) The elapsed time '(17 minutes)' — change from font-mono plain text to a styled pill: bg-panel border border-border rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 text-[10px] font-mono. (4) Add group to the story row button and use group-hover:bg-panel/50 for hover state. (5) While run is active, animate the progress bar (the w-full bg-accent bar) with a CSS animation: @keyframes shimmer using a gradient sweep, applied via animate-pulse or a custom class.
acceptanceCriteria: Each story row has a 4px left border whose color matches the story status
Escalation badges (Escalated: X→Y) are removed from collapsed row view and only appear in expanded detail
Reroute badges are removed from collapsed row and only appear in expanded detail
Elapsed time chip has pill styling (rounded, border, bg-panel)
Story rows have subtle hover background using group-hover
Progress bar animates with shimmer or pulse while run is in 'running' status
No regression on existing expand/collapse, token bar, or drag-to-reorder functionality

userStories.title: Wake search — highlight matched terms, show result count, and smart filter syntax
userStories.description: Improve the Wake/Archive page search in ArchivePanel.tsx. The FTS5 backend already supports full-text search. Frontend improvements: (1) Highlight the search query term within spec title text in the list — wrap matched substrings in a <mark> element styled with bg-accent/20 text-accent rounded-sm px-0.5 (case-insensitive match). Do this in a helper function highlightMatch(text: string, query: string): ReactNode. (2) Add a results count: below the search input, show 'X of Y specs' when query is active (use total from ArchiveResponse). (3) Auto-focus the search input on Wake panel mount (useEffect calling searchRef.current?.focus()). (4) Smart filter syntax: parse the search text for 'status:X' or 'tag:X' prefixes before setting the API params. E.g., if user types 'status:pending' extract status='pending' and set it as the statusFilter; remove that token from the search text before sending to the API. If user types 'tag:react' extract the tag and add it to tagFilter. Show a small chip below the input for each extracted filter with an X to remove it. (5) When search returns 0 results, show 'No specs matching "query"' with a Clear button.
acceptanceCriteria: Search terms are highlighted in spec titles in the list (case-insensitive, accent background)
A 'X results' or 'X of Y specs' count appears below the search field when query is active
Search input auto-focuses when Wake panel mounts
Typing 'status:pending' applies pending filter as a chip and removes that token from the search query
Typing 'tag:react' applies react tag filter as a chip and removes that token
Filter chips appear below the search input with X to remove each
Zero-results empty state shows the query text and a Clear button
All existing search, filter, and tag functionality is preserved (no regression)
300ms debounce is preserved

userStories.title: Providers page — model search input and filter chips
userStories.description: In SettingsPanel.tsx, the Providers tab Available Models section (found around the ExecutionEngineSection/ModelSection showing the 18 model cards grouped by provider) has no search or filter. Add: (1) A search input at the top of the Available Models section with placeholder 'Search models...'. As user types, filter the displayed models client-side (no API call) — match against model label, provider name, and model ID, case-insensitive. (2) Below the search input, add 4 filter pill buttons using the same pill/chip style as the Wake page tag filters: 'All' (default, shows all), 'Fast' (speedTier==='fast'), 'Cheap' (costTier==='low' or costTier==='free'), 'Large ctx' (contextWindow >= 500000). Active pill has accent background. Only one pill can be active at a time. (3) When a provider section has no matching models after search/filter, hide the entire provider section (header + models). (4) Add a count badge next to 'Available Models' heading: 'Available Models (X)' where X updates dynamically as filters change. (5) Add an X clear button when search input is non-empty.
acceptanceCriteria: Search input appears above model cards in Available Models section
Typing 'opus' instantly shows only models matching 'opus' in name/provider/id
Filter pills: All, Fast, Cheap, Large ctx — clicking each applies the corresponding filter
Only one speed/cost filter pill can be active at a time
Provider sections with no matching models are fully hidden (header + cards removed from DOM)
Model count badge 'Available Models (X)' updates as search/filter changes
Clear button (X) appears in search input when non-empty, clicking clears search
No regression: clicking model cards to set default, Test button, and other existing functionality

userStories.title: Skills panel — show 'Active in routing' badge and link to Context Settings
userStories.description: The main Skills panel (TemplateMarketplacePanel.tsx, sidebar Skills nav) and the Workspace Settings Context → Skills Manager (SkillsManager.tsx) show different data and confuse users. The Skills panel shows community/installed skills; the Context Skills shows .rorca/skills/ files used in context routing. Improvement: (1) In TemplateMarketplacePanel.tsx, after fetching the installed skills list, also call GET /api/workspaces/:id/skills (when workspaceId is available) to get the list of skills in .rorca/skills/. For each installed skill, if its name matches a .rorca/skills/ file, show a small green badge: inline-flex items-center gap-0.5 px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[9px] rounded bg-success/15 text-success border border-success/30 with text 'In routing'. (2) Add a footer note at the bottom of the installed skills list section (below the skill rows, above the search): 'Skills used in context routing are managed in Settings → Context → Skills.' Include a ChevronRight icon and make it a clickable link that navigates to the settings context tab (call onNavigate or use the existing workspace settings navigation with tab='context'). The footer note uses text-xs text-muted styling.
acceptanceCriteria: Skills panel fetches /api/workspaces/:id/skills when workspaceId is present
Installed skills whose name matches a .rorca/skills/ file show a green 'In routing' badge
Skills not in .rorca/skills/ show no routing badge
Footer note 'Skills used in context routing are managed in Settings → Context → Skills' appears below installed skills
Footer note is clickable and navigates to Settings context tab
Feature is gracefully hidden when no workspaceId is selected
No regression on existing skill install/uninstall/search functionality

userStories.title: Sidebar navigation typography — italic Wake label and refined nav styles
userStories.description: In src/components/Sidebar.tsx, the nav item labels use default font-sans at 13px. The user wants the 'Wake' label specifically to have a distinctive typographic treatment (italic, different weight) that reflects its archive/time-capsule concept. Changes: (1) In the NavLink component or wherever nav item labels are rendered, check if the current item's id === 'archive' (Wake) and apply an italic class: className includes italic font-medium. (2) For all nav labels, add font-medium weight (currently appears to be regular weight for inactive items). (3) Increase letter spacing slightly: tracking-[0.01em] on all nav labels. (4) For the 'rorca' logo text in the sidebar header, if it uses font-mono font-bold, maintain that but increase to text-[15px] and add a subtle text-accent color or gradient: bg-gradient-to-r from-accent to-accent/70 bg-clip-text text-transparent (if supported). (5) All changes must work in both light and dark theme variants.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Wake' nav label appears in italic style
All nav item labels use font-medium weight
Nav item labels have tracking-[0.01em] letter spacing
Logo 'rorca' text has refined styling (gradient or increased size, not breaking existing layout)
Both light and dark themes render correctly
No text overflow or layout regression in the sidebar
